newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEF'S TWO-TIME PRO BOWL OFFENSIVE TACKLE ALT RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEF'S TWO-TIME PRO BOWL OFFENSIVE TACKLE ALT RETIRES.

text.p: John Alt, a two-time Pro Bowl tackle and a fixture on the Kansas City Chiefs' offensive line for more than a decade, announced his retirement on Monday.

Alt, 35, played his entire career in Kansas City, after being selected in the first round of the 1984 draft. The native of Stuttgart, Germany appeared in 179 regular-season games and 10 playoff games in his 13-year career.
The announcement was made at the team's training camp.

The mammoth 6-8 (2.03 m), 307-pound (140 kg) lineman was named to the 1992 and 1993 Pro Bowls and is just one of just four Chiefs linemen to play at least 13 years with the team, joining Ed Budde, Jim Tyrer and Jack Rudnay.
Alt had a string of 94 straight starts ended in 1994 due to a back injury. In 1995 he received the Ed Block Courage Award, given to players that battle injuries and hardship.
Alt played in 12 games and started 11 last season. His 179 games is second among Chiefs offensive lineman to Tyrer, who played in 180.
